title: Regional attenuation controller for request pacing and model fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We need an automated, region-aware controller that attenuates incoming request load (request pacing) and triggers safe fallback to pre-computed model variants when regional capacity signals indicate overload. Goals: 1) Detect overload patterns (429 burst, request timeouts, elevated error-rate) at region and tier granularity; 2) Apply a soft attenuation (request pacing + token-level batching adjustment) before hard cutovers to preserve quality; 3) If severity persists, trigger deterministic fallback to lower-cost/quantized model variants or cross-region reroute per tenant routing policy; 4) Provide observability and a controlled rollout path with canary and automatic rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Controller exposes per-region/tier thresholds and a decay window configurable via routing policy
On 10% sustained elevation of 429 rate above baseline for 60s, controller applies soft attenuation (max concurrent requests reduced by X) and emits signal to routing plane

If timeouts or 5xx error-rate exceed configured hard threshold for 3 consecutive windows, controller flips to fallback variant with a staged traffic shift (10%->50%->100%) and records telemetry for each step
Canary rollout to a subset of tenants (by weight) with automatic rollback if cost/latency/quality regressions exceed SLOs
End-to-end testing harness and chaos tests that exercise 429 bursts, simulated GPU OOMs, and network partitions
Dashboards show attenuation factor, variant-fanout percentage, incident correlation, and tenant impact within 1 minute of signal
design_notes: We will implement a small controller service colocated in routing plane that subscribes to regional telemetry (p50/p95 latency, 429 rate, timeout rate, 5xx rate, queue depth). The controller computes a composite overload score using an exponential decay window and a tunable hysteresis band. Trade-offs: - Conservative thresholds reduce false positives but increase exposure to overload; - Aggressive fallbacks reduce customer-visible errors but may degrade model output quality. To minimize quality regression we prefer staged fanout to quantized variants and add prompt-preserving filters for long-form generation. The controller will prefabricate commands consumed by the route-manager for deterministic cutovers. Security: controller actions are auditable and signed; only routes in the same tenant-scope can trigger tenant-targeted fallbacks.
implementation_plan: 1) Telemetry: augment regional metrics pipeline to emit normalized 429/timeouts/error-rate signals (ETA: 1 week). 2) Controller: implement scoring function and REST API to publish attenuation directives (ETA: 2 weeks). 3) Routing integration: route-manager applies attenuation and variant fanout (ETA: 1 week). 4) Canary: run in passive mode for 48h, then enable active mitigation for a small tenant cohort (ETA: 3 days). 5) Full rollout and post-launch tuning (ETA: 1 week).
rollout_strategy: Phase 0: Observability only (no actions). Phase 1: Passive canary where controller suggests actions in logs. Phase 2: Small active canary (5% of traffic for selected tenants). Phase 3: Regional enablement with automatic rollback on quality/cost/latency regressions. Failure modes: if route-manager fails to apply directives, controller will escalate via alerting and mark region degraded; fallback to global conservative circuit-breaker.
telemetry_and_alerting: Emit the following metrics: regional_overload_score, attenuation_factor, variant_fanout_pct, local_429_rate, local_timeout_rate, local_5xx_rate, tenant_impact_count. Alerts: overload_score>0.8 for >120s; canary_quality_regression>threshold; rollout_rollback_triggered. Wire to Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/route-controller/attenuation-panel
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring and hysteresis; integration tests using local telemetry replay harness; chaos tests that simulate: 1) 3x spike in 429s, 2) sustained timeout surge, 3) GPU OOM on model variant nodes. QA checklist includes verifying staged fanout percentages and audit log entries for every directive.
